name: Final value of a lump-sum investment
formel: Final value = K x (1 + i)^n
erklaerung: The formula shows the amount to which capital invested as a lump sum grows at a constant interest rate.
variablen: interest rate per period as a decimal, 5% = 0.05

name: Present value
formel: Present value = Final value / (1 + i)^n
erklaerung: The present value discounts a future amount back to today. This makes payments at different points in time comparable.

name: Effective interest rate with intra-year compounding
formel: i_eff = (1 + i_nom / m)^m - 1
erklaerung: The effective interest rate makes offers with monthly, quarterly or annual crediting of interest comparable.
variablen: number of interest periods per year

name: Final value of a savings plan (payments in arrears)
formel: Final value = R x ((1 + i)^n - 1) / i
erklaerung: The formula gives the final capital of a savings plan with a constant contribution that is paid in at the end of each period.

name: Final value of a savings plan (payments in advance)
formel: Final value = R x ((1 + i)^n - 1) / i x (1 + i)
erklaerung: The same calculation applies to payments at the start of each period, with each contribution earning interest for one period longer.

name: Contribution required for a savings goal
erklaerung: The formula gives the contribution, paid in arrears, that leads to the target capital by the end of the term.

name: Time needed to reach the target capital
formel: n = ln(Z / K) / ln(1 + i)
erklaerung: The formula calculates how many periods a lump-sum investment needs to reach the target amount.

name: CAGR (compound annual growth rate)
formel: CAGR = (Final value / Initial value)^(1 / n) - 1
erklaerung: The CAGR condenses performance over several years into a single annual return. It is identical to the geometric mean.
variablen: value at the end of the period

name: Rule of 72 (doubling time)
formel: Doubling time in years = 72 / Interest rate as a percentage
erklaerung: This mental arithmetic approximation for the doubling of capital is sufficiently accurate for interest rates between 4% and 12%.
variablen: annual return as a whole number, that is, 8 instead of 0.08

name: Real interest rate according to Fisher
formel: r_real = (1 + r_nom) / (1 + p) - 1
erklaerung: The formula removes inflation from the nominal return exactly. The common subtraction r_nom minus p is only an approximation.
variablen: real return, that is, the increase in purchasing power

name: Arithmetic mean of returns
formel: r_arith = (r1 + r2 + ... + rn) / n
erklaerung: The arithmetic mean estimates the expected return of a single future period. It overstates the growth in wealth actually achieved over several periods.

name: Geometric mean of returns
erklaerung: The geometric mean gives the return actually achieved per period. Only this return, multiplied over time, leads correctly to the final wealth.

name: Volatility drag
formel: r_geo (approximation) = r_arith - sigma^2 / 2
erklaerung: The approximation quantifies how much fluctuations push the return actually achieved below the arithmetic average.

name: Recovery after a loss
formel: Required gain = 1 / (1 - v) - 1
erklaerung: The formula shows the asymmetry of losses. Minus 50% requires plus 100%, minus 20% only plus 25%.

name: Standard deviation (sample)
formel: sigma = sqrt( sum (r_t - r_bar)^2 / (n - 1) )
erklaerung: The standard deviation is the usual measure of the volatility of returns and the basis of almost all other risk metrics.

name: Covariance and correlation
formel: Cov(A,B) = sum (rA_t - rA_bar) x (rB_t - rB_bar) / (n - 1); rho = Cov(A,B) / (sigma_A x sigma_B)
erklaerung: Covariance measures the co-movement of two investments. Correlation normalises it to the range minus 1 to plus 1 and determines how much diversification reduces risk.
variablen: returns of investments A and B in period t
standard deviations of the two investments

name: Annualising volatility
formel: sigma_year = sigma_period x sqrt(T)
erklaerung: The formula converts measures of fluctuation to an annual basis, for example monthly values with sqrt(12) or daily values with sqrt(252).
variablen: standard deviation of the period returns

name: Sharpe ratio
formel: Sharpe = (Rp - Rf) / sigma_p
erklaerung: The Sharpe ratio measures the excess return over the risk-free rate per unit of total risk. It is only meaningful when comparing similar investments over the same period.

name: Sortino ratio
formel: Sortino = (Rp - T) / DD with DD = sqrt( sum min(r_t - T, 0)^2 / n )
erklaerung: The Sortino ratio works like the Sharpe ratio, but counts only downward deviations as risk and not the upward swings, which do investors no harm.

name: Maximum drawdown
formel: MDD = (Trough after the peak - Peak) / Peak
erklaerung: The maximum drawdown is the largest interim decline from peak to trough and therefore the risk measure that describes the limit of what an investor can bear in practice.
variablen: highest level of the portfolio so far
lowest level after that, before a new high is reached

name: Portfolio return
formel: E(Rp) = w1 x E(R1) + w2 x E(R2) + ... + wn x E(Rn)
erklaerung: The expected return of a portfolio is the weighted average of the individual returns, and no diversification effect arises here.
variablen: proportion of investment i in the portfolio, sum of all wi = 1

name: Portfolio variance for two investments
formel: sigma_p^2 = wA^2 x sigmaA^2 + wB^2 x sigmaB^2 + 2 x wA x wB x sigmaA x sigmaB x rho
erklaerung: The formula shows why the risk of a portfolio lies below the weighted average of the individual risks as soon as the correlation is less than 1.

name: Portfolio variance for n investments
formel: sigma_p^2 = sum over i sum over j ( wi x wj x Cov(i,j) )
erklaerung: The formula is the general form of portfolio variance. With n investments, the n x (n - 1) covariances outweigh the n individual variances.
variablen: proportions of investments i and j
covariance between i and j, the variance for i = j

name: Portfolio variance with equal weighting
formel: sigma_p^2 = (1 / n) x Average variance + ((n - 1) / n) x Average covariance
erklaerung: The formula shows the limit of diversification. As the number of holdings rises, the variance term disappears, while the average covariance remains as market risk.

name: Beta
formel: Beta = Cov(Ri, Rm) / Var(Rm)
erklaerung: Beta measures the sensitivity of an investment to market movements. A beta of 1 means moving in line with the market.

name: CAPM (expected return)
formel: E(Ri) = Rf + Beta x (E(Rm) - Rf)
erklaerung: The CAPM derives the expected return solely from the market risk that cannot be diversified away and thus provides the cost of equity.

name: Jensen's alpha
formel: Alpha = Rp - ( Rf + Beta x (Rm - Rf) )
erklaerung: Alpha is the part of the return that is not explained by the market risk taken, that is, the performance of the management.

name: Gordon growth (dividend discount model)
formel: P = D1 / (k - g)
erklaerung: The model values a stream of payments that grows at a constant rate forever. It also serves as the terminal value formula in the DCF.
variablen: required return or cost of capital
perpetual growth rate, necessarily lower than k

name: DCF present value
formel: Enterprise value = sum ( FCF_t / (1 + WACC)^t ) + TV / (1 + WACC)^n with TV = FCF_(n+1) / (WACC - g)
erklaerung: The DCF method is the central valuation approach. The enterprise value is the sum of all discounted future free cash flows plus the discounted terminal value.
variablen: free cash flow in year t
terminal value after the detailed planning period

name: WACC (weighted average cost of capital)
formel: WACC = E / (E + D) x k_E + D / (E + D) x k_D x (1 - s)
erklaerung: The WACC is the discount rate of a DCF. Debt is included after tax because interest reduces the tax burden.
variablen: cost of equity, usually from the CAPM

name: Free cash flow to the firm
formel: FCFF = EBIT x (1 - s) + Depreciation and amortisation - Capital expenditure - Change in working capital
erklaerung: The FCFF is the cash flow to which all providers of capital are entitled. It is the input of the DCF method at the level of the company as a whole and is discounted at the WACC. In the equity version, it is replaced by the free cash flow to equity (FCFE), discounted at the cost of equity.
variablen: cash spent on property, plant and equipment and on intangible assets
inventories plus receivables minus trade payables

name: Owner earnings according to Buffett
formel: Owner earnings = Reported earnings + Depreciation, amortisation and other non-cash charges - Average annual maintenance capex
erklaerung: Owner earnings approximate the amount an owner can take out without weakening the company's competitive position.
variablen: net profit according to the financial statements
investment to maintain the existing business, necessarily an estimate according to Buffett

name: ROIC (return on invested capital)
formel: ROIC = NOPAT / Invested capital with NOPAT = EBIT x (1 - s)
erklaerung: ROIC shows how productively a company uses all the capital employed. Value is created only if ROIC is above the WACC.
variablen: equity plus interest-bearing debt minus excess cash

name: Sustainable growth
formel: g = ROIC x Reinvestment rate
erklaerung: Sustainable growth is the product of the return on capital and the proportion of profit that is reinvested. It therefore cannot be assumed freely.
variablen: proportion of profit that is reinvested in the company

name: Price-to-earnings ratio (P/E)
formel: P/E = Price per share / Earnings per share
erklaerung: The P/E ratio gives the price per unit of earnings. Its reciprocal is the earnings yield. The P/E ratio can only be compared meaningfully within one industry.
variablen: net profit divided by the number of shares

name: Price-to-book ratio (P/B)
formel: P/B = Price per share / Book value per share
erklaerung: The P/B ratio relates the market price to the equity on the balance sheet. A P/B ratio above 1 is justified if the return on equity is above the cost of equity.
variablen: equity divided by the number of shares

name: EV / EBIT
formel: EV / EBIT with EV = Market capitalisation + Net financial debt
erklaerung: The ratio values the company as a whole, regardless of its financing structure. Companies with different levels of debt can be compared better with it than with the P/E ratio.
variablen: enterprise value, the total value of the company
share price times number of shares
interest-bearing debt minus cash and cash equivalents

name: Three-step DuPont
formel: ROE = (Net profit / Revenue) x (Revenue / Balance sheet total) x (Balance sheet total / Equity)
erklaerung: The formula breaks down the return on equity into margin, asset turnover and leverage and thus shows where the return comes from.
variablen: equity multiplier, that is, the leverage

name: Piotroski F-score
formel: F-score = sum of 9 yes/no points: 4 on profitability, 3 on leverage and liquidity, 2 on operating efficiency
erklaerung: The F-score is a points system that separates companies with sound balance sheets from struggling ones within a value universe. Scores of 8 to 9 points are considered strong, 0 to 2 weak.
variablen: including positive profit, positive operating cash flow, rising return on capital, cash flow above profit
falling debt, rising liquidity, no capital increase
rising gross margin, rising asset turnover

name: Altman Z-score
erklaerung: The Z-score estimates the insolvency risk of listed industrial companies. A value above 2.99 is considered safe, 1.81 to 2.99 a grey area and below 1.81 at risk.
variablen: market value of equity / book value of liabilities

name: Bond price (present value)
erklaerung: The fair price is the present value of all coupons and the redemption payment. If y rises, P falls.
variablen: price, which plus accrued interest gives the amount payable

name: Current yield
formel: Current yield = Coupon / Price
erklaerung: The current yield is a rough income measure that only captures the ongoing interest payment and ignores the price gain or loss up to maturity.
variablen: annual interest payment in currency units

name: Yield to maturity (approximation)
formel: YTM (approximation) = ( C + (N - P) / n ) / ( (N + P) / 2 )
erklaerung: The approximation estimates the total return to maturity without iteration. Strictly speaking, the YTM is the interest rate at which the present value of all payments equals the price.

name: Macaulay duration
formel: D = sum ( t x CF_t / (1 + y)^t ) / P
erklaerung: The Macaulay duration is the present-value-weighted average period for which capital is tied up, in years, and at the same time the horizon at which price risk and reinvestment risk offset each other.
variablen: time of the payment in years
price, that is, the present value of all payments

name: Modified duration
formel: D_mod = D / (1 + y); Price change as a percentage = -D_mod x dy
erklaerung: The modified duration translates duration into a direct price response. A bond with a D_mod of 7 loses around 7% if interest rates rise by one percentage point.
variablen: change in interest rates in percentage points, as a decimal

name: Convexity adjustment
formel: Price change = -D_mod x dy + 0.5 x C x dy^2
erklaerung: The formula corrects the error of linear duration for larger jumps in interest rates. Positive convexity always works in the investor's favour.
variablen: change in interest rates as a decimal

name: Accrued interest
formel: Accrued interest = Coupon x (Days since the last payment / Days in the interest period)
erklaerung: With accrued interest, the buyer compensates the seller for the interest that has accumulated up to the day before the value date (settlement date) but has not yet been paid out.
variablen: depending on the day count convention, act/act according to ICMA for German federal bonds

name: Break-even inflation
formel: Break-even inflation = Yield of the nominal bond - Yield of the inflation-linked bond
erklaerung: Break-even inflation shows the average inflation over the term that is priced in by the market. The indexed bond only pays off if inflation is higher than that.
variablen: same remaining maturity and same issuer required

name: d1 and d2 (Black-Scholes)
formel: d1 = ( ln(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 x sigma^2) x T ) / (sigma x sqrt(T)); d2 = d1 - sigma x sqrt(T)
erklaerung: Both values are auxiliary quantities of the Black-Scholes formula. Under the risk-neutral measure, N(d2) is the probability that the call expires in the money.

name: Black-Scholes: call
formel: C = S x e^(-q x T) x N(d1) - K x e^(-r x T) x N(d2)
erklaerung: The formula gives the fair price of a European call option. In practice, it is applied the other way round to derive the implied volatility from the market price.
variablen: cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution

name: Black-Scholes: put
formel: P = K x e^(-r x T) x N(-d2) - S x e^(-q x T) x N(-d1)
erklaerung: The formula gives the fair price of a European put option under the same assumptions as for the call.
variablen: cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution
auxiliary quantities of the Black-Scholes formula

name: Put-call parity
formel: C + K x e^(-r x T) = P + S x e^(-q x T)
erklaerung: Put-call parity is a model-free arbitrage relationship between call, put, underlying and bond. Any violation would allow a risk-free profit.

name: Delta
formel: Delta_Call = e^(-q x T) x N(d1); Delta_Put = Delta_Call - e^(-q x T)
erklaerung: Delta is the change in the option price per unit change in the price of the underlying and also the hedge ratio. At the money, it is around 0.5 for a call and around minus 0.5 for a put.

name: Gamma
formel: Gamma = e^(-q x T) x N'(d1) / (S x sigma x sqrt(T))
erklaerung: Gamma is the change in delta per price movement of the underlying. It is identical for call and put and greatest at the money shortly before expiry.
variablen: density of the standard normal distribution at d1

name: Vega
formel: Vega = S x e^(-q x T) x N'(d1) x sqrt(T)
erklaerung: The formula gives the change in price for a change in volatility of one unit, that is, 100 percentage points. The usual vega per percentage point is one hundredth of that. It is identical for call and put and rises with a longer time to expiry.
variablen: density of the standard normal distribution

name: Theta (call)
formel: Theta_Call = -S x N'(d1) x sigma x e^(-q x T) / (2 x sqrt(T)) - r x K x e^(-r x T) x N(d2) + q x S x e^(-q x T) x N(d1)
erklaerung: Theta is the loss of time value per unit of time. For the buyer, it is usually negative and strongest in the last weeks before expiry.

name: Annuity
erklaerung: The formula gives the constant instalment of an annuity loan. With each payment, its composition shifts from interest to repayment.
variablen: interest rate per period, for monthly payments the annual rate divided by 12

name: Outstanding balance after k periods
erklaerung: The formula shows the debt still outstanding at the end of the fixed-rate period and thus how large the follow-up financing has to be.

name: Term of an annuity loan
formel: n = -ln( 1 - S0 x i / R ) / ln(1 + i)
erklaerung: The formula calculates the total term until the loan is fully repaid. If S0 x i is greater than or equal to R, the loan is never repaid.

name: Gross rental yield
formel: Gross rental yield = Annual net basic rent / Purchase price
erklaerung: The gross rental yield is used for a first rough assessment of a property. It ignores incidental purchase costs, running costs and vacancy and is therefore systematically too high.
variablen: basic rent excluding service charges, times 12
purchase price alone, excluding incidental costs

name: Net rental yield
formel: Net rental yield = (Annual net basic rent - Non-recoverable costs) / (Purchase price + Incidental purchase costs)
erklaerung: The net rental yield is the reliable yield figure because it takes into account incidental acquisition costs, management, maintenance and the rent loss allowance (Mietausfallwagnis).
variablen: management, maintenance reserve (Instandhaltungsrücklage), rent loss allowance
real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer), notary and land register, estate agent's commission where applicable

name: Price-to-rent ratio (multiplier)
formel: Price-to-rent ratio = Purchase price / Annual net basic rent
erklaerung: The price-to-rent ratio is the reciprocal of the gross rental yield. A ratio of 25 corresponds to 4% gross, a ratio of 40 to only 2.5%.
variablen: always the basic rent, never the rent including heating

name: Leverage effect
formel: r_E = r_A + (r_A - i_D) x (D / E)
erklaerung: Debt increases the return on equity as long as the return on total capital is above the loan interest rate. If it is below, debt reduces the return on equity just as strongly.
variablen: return on total capital of the property

name: Flat-rate withholding tax (Abgeltungsteuer) with solidarity surcharge
formel: Tax = Income x 0.25 x 1.055 = Income x 0.26375
erklaerung: The formula gives the standard tax burden on capital income without church tax, which the bank withholds directly as capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer).
variablen: capital income after deducting the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag)
special tax rate under Section 32d(1) EStG (Income Tax Act)
solidarity surcharge of 5.5% on the tax

name: Capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer) with church tax reduction
formel: Capital income withholding tax = (e - 4 x q) / (4 + k)
erklaerung: Church tax on capital income taxed at the flat rate is not deductible as a special expense (Sonderausgabe; Section 10(1) no. 4 EStG, Income Tax Act). Instead, the tax is reduced by 25% of the church tax attributable to the capital income (Section 32d(1) sentences 3 and 4 EStG). This is why the tax rate falls from 25% to 24.45% at k = 0.09.
variablen: church tax rate, 0.08 in Bavaria and Baden-Württemberg, otherwise 0.09

name: Total burden including church tax
formel: Total burden = Capital income withholding tax rate x (1 + 0.055 + k)
erklaerung: Capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer), solidarity surcharge and church tax together come to around 27.99% at k = 0.09 and around 27.82% at k = 0.08.

name: Advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale)
formel: Base return = Redemption price on the first valuation day of the year x Base interest rate x 0.7; Advance lump sum = Base return - Distributions, at most the increase in value during the year
erklaerung: The advance lump sum is used to tax a flat-rate minimum return, above all for accumulating funds. For distributing funds, it arises to the extent that the year's distributions are below the base return. If the fund falls in value, the advance lump sum is zero.
variablen: (Basiszins) determined by the Bundesbank and published by the Federal Ministry of Finance (BMF), 3.20% as of 2 January 2026
flat-rate cost deduction under Section 18 InvStG (Investment Tax Act)

name: Partial exemption (Teilfreistellung)
formel: Taxable income = Gross income x (1 - Partial exemption rate)
erklaerung: The partial exemption compensates on a flat-rate basis for the tax already borne at fund level. It applies equally to distributions, the advance lump sum (Vorabpauschale) and capital gains.
variablen: equity funds 0.30, mixed funds 0.15, real estate funds 0.60, foreign real estate funds 0.80, other funds 0

name: Tax after the saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag)
formel: Tax = max(Income - Saver's allowance, 0) x Tax rate
erklaerung: The allowance is only taken into account in the tax deduction if the bank holds an exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag).
variablen: total of all capital income after partial exemption
€1,000 per person, €2,000 for joint assessment (as of 2026)

name: Return after tax and inflation
formel: r_net_real = (1 + r x (1 - s)) / (1 + p) - 1
erklaerung: Only this measure of return is decisive, because it shows how much purchasing power remains after tax has been deducted.

name: Annual withdrawal based on the withdrawal rate
formel: Annual withdrawal = Starting capital x Withdrawal rate
erklaerung: The formula is the basic form of the 4% rule. The amount withdrawn in the first year is then only adjusted for inflation.
variablen: portfolio value at the start of retirement
3% to 4% according to the Trinity study for 30 years, closer to 3.25% to 3.5% for very long horizons

name: Capital required for permanent withdrawals
formel: Capital = Annual withdrawal / Withdrawal rate
erklaerung: According to this reciprocal rule, 25 times annual spending is needed at 4%, and around 29 times at 3.5%.

name: Capital required for a limited withdrawal period
formel: Capital = E x (1 - (1 + r)^(-n)) / r
erklaerung: The formula gives the present value of an annuity for a fixed period. If the calculation uses a real return, the purchasing power of the withdrawal is preserved.
variablen: real return after costs and taxes

name: Withdrawal period for a given amount of capital
formel: n = -ln( 1 - K x r / E ) / ln(1 + r)
erklaerung: The formula shows how long a portfolio lasts with a fixed withdrawal. If K x r is greater than or equal to E, it lasts indefinitely in mathematical terms.

name: Purchasing power after n years
formel: Real purchasing power = Amount / (1 + p)^n
erklaerung: The formula converts a future nominal amount into today's purchasing power and thus makes the effect of inflation over long periods visible.

name: Dynamic withdrawal
formel: Annual withdrawal = Current portfolio value x Fixed percentage
erklaerung: The withdrawal is based on the portfolio value. As a result, the portfolio can mathematically never be used up; in return, the available income fluctuates with the market.
variablen: value at the start of the withdrawal year

name: Position size based on risk per trade
formel: Number of units = (Portfolio value x Risk per trade) / (Entry price - Stop price)
erklaerung: The formula derives the position size from the maximum loss accepted instead of choosing the stake by gut feeling.
variablen: proportion of the portfolio that is lost if the trade ends in a loss, usually 0.005 to 0.02
loss per unit when the stop is triggered

name: Expected value per trade
formel: EV = p x Average gain - (1 - p) x Average loss
erklaerung: The formula shows whether a strategy has a positive expected value at all. Without one, any position sizing rule merely leads to a loss more slowly.
variablen: mean gain of the winning trades
mean loss of the losing trades

name: Kelly criterion
formel: f = ( p x b - (1 - p) ) / b
erklaerung: The Kelly criterion determines the fraction of capital per bet that maximises long-term geometric growth. Because of estimation errors, usually only half of it is used in practice.
variablen: optimal fraction of capital per bet
gain per unit staked if successful

name: Reward-to-risk ratio
formel: RRR = (Target price - Entry price) / (Entry price - Stop price)
erklaerung: The RRR relates the targeted gain to the risk taken. It is only meaningful together with the win rate.
variablen: planned exit in the event of a profit
exit in the event of a loss

name: Minimum win rate for break-even
formel: p_min = 1 / (1 + RRR)
erklaerung: The formula shows the minimum win rate that a reward-to-risk ratio requires. At an RRR of 2, 33.3% is enough; at an RRR of 1, 50% is needed.
variablen: win rate at or above which the strategy no longer loses money before costs
